title: Using Scopus and OpenAlex APIs for Bibliographic Data Retrieval
author: Harder
materials: the scholarly APIs to tap into, (

steps.title: Initialize stage and prepare IDs
steps.instruction: For Stage A, place the search query strings as input. For Stages B‑E, use the record IDs obtained from the previous stage; save these IDs in a plain‑text file named ‘IDs.txt’, which will serve as input for the next stage.

steps.title: Retrieve records via API
steps.instruction: Call the appropriate scholarly API (Scopus Search API or OpenAlex Search API for Stage A; Works/Abstract Retrieval API for Stage B; Affiliation Retrieval API for Stage C; Author Retrieval API for Stage D; Serial Title Retrieval API for Stage E) and download the records identified by the IDs. For the search APIs, store only the record IDs; for the retrieval APIs, store the full record payloads.

steps.title: Create SQL INSERT statements
steps.instruction: Transform each retrieved record into an SQL INSERT command that matches the target MySQL table schema (e.g., works, institutions, authors, sources). Use the example SQL shown in Box 8 as a template and generate one INSERT statement per record.

steps.title: Insert records into MySQL database
steps.instruction: Execute the generated INSERT statements against the local MySQL database (developed on macOS; compatible with UNIX or Windows). This step loads the retrieved bibliographic data into permanent tables for further processing.

steps.title: Process records to extract fields
steps.instruction: Query the populated tables to extract the relevant data elements (e.g., titles, abstracts, affiliation IDs, author IDs, source titles) and format them as needed for downstream analysis.

steps.title: Store extracted elements locally
steps.instruction: Write the extracted data elements to a temporary local repository (e.g., CSV or JSON files) in accordance with the APIs’ use terms and conditions. Optionally, run Bash batch files that invoke the SQL code to store these elements, as illustrated in Box 8.
